commenti.body:
Such a great movie. Pacino just released his book, and I think he said he donated all his salary from this movie to the gay movement. I hope that's true.


I also hope he discusses the themes. I personally always interpreted the ending as him being conflicted with his sexual orientation. Or, rather, that's what the entire movie is really about.

I’ve def read interpretations that Pacino was the killer motivated by advancing his career (and maybe also internalized gay panic). I watched earlier this year and I like that interpretation. The end definitely suggests things are not as they seem on the surface.

I never heard this theory. It's interesting but I'm not sure there's enough meat in the evidence to support it. I've only seen the movie once though. I always took it as you did; that it was open to whether they caught the actual killer and that Pacino's character was struggling with his sexual orientation.

There is some deliberate ambivalence to the whole film, not only in what's going on in Pacino's head, but also whether there is actually one connected murder series, or if the film is a reflection on gay panic in general. One example is how Friedkin shot every murder with a different actor as the killer. It's a trick that was copied over 20 years later by David Fincher in *Zodiac*.

One of my all time favorites. I interpreted it as there possibly being more than one killer as well as Burns possibly being the one who killed his neighbor. For me it works so well without any concrete explanation, the fact that burns and the killer who is caught at the end are dressed exactly the same, Burns somehow knows the lullaby that the killer sings. So many little details that make it truly a masterpiece IMO.

In the film, the killer's identity shifts but it's heavily implied that Pacino has been affected by it all and has killed (maybe not for the first time).  The late great Robin Wood has a brilliant essay discussing Cruising and Looking for Mr. Goodbar as narratives that are incoherent yet fascinating in the way they refuse to clarify or resolve their idiosyncrasies and contradictions.  The message I take from Cruising is that the killer is more Patriarchy (in the guise of the unpleasant Father/Boss) than one specific person.

But then why wouldn’t he just have helped the cops pin it all on Skip Lee? He was reluctant to name him the killer. The cops were ready to pin it on him even with little evidence. Also wouldn’t Pacino’s fingerprints be on file since he’s a cop? I find it hard to believe that he would kill all these random dark haired men and then kill light haired Ted who he was actually friends with. I don’t know I don’t want to believe that Pacino was the killer. Repressed gay feelings probably but I don’t think he was the killer.
